newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady on Friday in moderate trade with most traders sidelined due mainly to the absence of fresh incentives, dealers said.
Activity was limited by a shortage of players in the market because of the long Independence Day holiday weekend, they said.

"Rates were steady to easier in the morning on some position adjustments. Narrow range trade dominated trade partly because of the holiday in the U.S. and partly because there are no (U.S. economic) indicators coming out tonight," a local dealer said.
"Market activity was also thin because most people have squared or are squaring their positionns ahead of the weekend," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday was unchanged from Thursday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent. Week-fixed eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among term rates, one-month was unchanged from Thursday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8, nine-months eased 1/16 point to 5-15/16 5-13/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent.
